newsitem.title: ITALY: Size of Italy's ENI offer could be increased.
newsitem.headline: Size of Italy's ENI offer could be increased.

text.p: Italy's offer of up to 805 million shares in the second tranche sale of state energy group ENI could be increased if market interest is strong, senior Italian Treasury Ministry official Mario Draghi said on Monday.

Draghi, the ministry's director general, told a news conference that a further offer could also be made within the next nine months if market interest persisted and global coordinators saw no negative impact on the share price.

The Treasury announced on Sunday that it was offering a total of 700 million ordinary shares in ENI, with a maximum 105 million available for offer to institutional investors under a "green shoe" arrangement

"If the market interest is still sustained, then one could think of increasing the offer," Draghi told a news conference. He valued the offer, excluding the "green shoe", at 5.1 trillion lire at the current share price.
Sunday's announcement said a minimum of 250 million of the ordinary shares would be offered in a public sale offer (OPV) of which up to 25 percent was destined for ENI employees.

Vittorio Serafino, deputy director of merchant bank IMI, which is helping to coordinate the sale, said the sale prospectus provided for the Treasury to assign the entire offer to the public if there was strong demand, with additional shares offered to institutional investors.
